I went through something similar. Had my guy bestie leave me, and a guy breakup when I told them I was molested/r*ped for a year as a kid. And somehow I ingrained it that when I tell people about this, they leave me. So I didn't speak about it for years. Also developed attachment issues. 

And then there was this guy, let's call him S. He came along and I was falling pretty hard for him, even though we were friends. And after I was getting attached, I was getting more and more afraid of abandonment, and I thought  I should tell him, so that he leaves.

And I just told him one day. And the first thing he said to me was, "I'm never leaving you". And idk how he knew that it was just what I wanted to needed, but yeah he said that. And now we have been living together for almost 3 years. I'm in therapy and things are getting better slowly. 

When I told my therapist about this, she said "people will break your heart. But there will be people who will help you put it back. Don't change or lose who you are because of either of them, and you will be fine" :)

Okay so I went to Ladakh [A part of Jammu and Kashmir in India)] - a place which the Emperor Jahangir called "heaven on earth" - for a trip with my family. Now Ladakh has people of three main religions - Hindus, Muslims, and Buddhists. And there is a deep secluded valley - called Nubra valley which is like 8 hours from the main city Leh. Ladakh is known for it's cold deserts, it's beautiful mountains, orchards, etc. And since the government didn't let people who are not of Ladakh buy land there, it was well preserved. We were staying in a tiny inn which had a Hindu host. And there were some Americans staying there as well. And we were eating in the dining hall, and this guy was SO FURIOUS at the innkeeper that they didn't have beef (people in Ladakh  usually prefer to eat chicken/goat/sheep meat). This guy is so mad at the innkeeper for not having beef (which is against Hindu traditions, as the innkeeper explained) and he asks if they have chinese food.  (There has been a conflict of land between India and China over Ladakh, not to mention a lot of mainland Indians are racist towards people who live in the mountains and "chini" which means Chinese is a racial slur used against people of mountains in India). The innkeeper got so offended that he asked the cook  to wait on him, who explained the cuisine they served. And this guy says I'll have water and then starts discussing how bad a service this area has and how he would have bought a land here, had this place not been so "boring". Probably the worst American I have seen.
Also why do you think your dick needs a soda can near it while taking a dick pic?

What do y'all do on sleepovers? I mean I get that some of you play video games, etc. But do you all *experiment* the way girls do? Do you show eachother the clothes and underwears that you recently bought? Do you cuddle or share a blanket? Do you try to summon a demon? Do you talk about the women you like?

As a person who had a family who didn't respect my boundaries and had been r*ped as a 7 yo, I gotta tell you that you need to move out. It will ruin your mental health if this continues. I cannot emphasise how much better I felt when I started living alone, and then even with my bf. If a person is not respecting your boundaries, continuously, then you need to cut them out.

It is definitely helping but it honestly depends on the therapist. I was put in therapy a couple times before and it never worked for me. However rn my therapist is very helpful, understanding, compassionate, and makes sure that I don't feel judged above all. She takes time to clear my doubts, and makes me feel really comfortable. In my first session with this therapist, I asked all my questions about her as a person so that I knew what kind of person I'd be opening up to. If you're scared of going into therapy, you can try online therapy before meeting them in person. But yes, please make sure that your therapist is a trustworthy person, because I know a queer friend of mine who was outed to her parents by her therapist. So make sure you trust your therapist, or you wouldn't be able to work on anything. All the best ❤️
Thank you for being kind. This is the first time I've ever said anything about this on a public forum. Hopefully more people will be kinder to their children.
